$comment: What every binding (the Node.js addon and the web module) must expose. Checked by `mise run surface`, which `mise run test` runs: each public function of include/tinyactors/*.h is "bind" (it survives linking every binding with dead-code elimination from its entry points), bound for some bindings with a reason for the others, or skipped with a reason; each typings file declares every runtime export and public class member of the module it describes. A new TA_API function fails the check until it is classified here.

ta_trace_body_size.skip: for C hosts that copy records; the bindings hand records to the OTLP encoder (ta_otlp_read), which reads bodies itself

ta_core_deliver.skip: kernel-only embedding (bring your own scheduler); the bindings embed ta_system

ta_datamodel_environment_charge.skip: JS datamodel work is not metered: the core charges each datamodel call a fixed fuel cost, and the JS run loop keeps slices short by adapting the fuel budget to wall time (SLICE_MS)

ta_datamodel_environment_chart.skip: the bindings' datamodels keep the chart of each instance themselves

ta_datamodel_environment_image.skip: the bindings' datamodels keep the image of each instance themselves

ta_datamodel_null.skip: bound implicitly: ta_system_init adds the null datamodel when the host does not

ta_datamodel_ecmascript_binding.skip: the C ECMAScript datamodel (quickjs-ng) is for C hosts; the JS bindings evaluate ECMAScript with their own engine (bindings/shared)

ta_datamodel_ecmascript_eval_json.skip: C ECMAScript datamodel; the JS bindings evaluate ECMAScript with their own engine

ta_datamodel_ecmascript_free.skip: C ECMAScript datamodel; the JS bindings evaluate ECMAScript with their own engine

ta_datamodel_ecmascript_heap_bytes.skip: C ECMAScript datamodel; the JS bindings evaluate ECMAScript with their own engine

ta_datamodel_ecmascript_js_runtime.skip: C ECMAScript datamodel; the JS bindings evaluate ECMAScript with their own engine

ta_datamodel_ecmascript_new.skip: C ECMAScript datamodel; the JS bindings evaluate ECMAScript with their own engine

ta_datamodel_ecmascript_payload_from_jso.skip: C ECMAScript datamodel; JS payloads are JS values

ta_datamodel_ecmascript_payload_to_json.skip: C ECMAScript datamodel; JS payloads are JS values

ta_datamodel_ecmascript_payload_eval.skip: C ECMAScript datamodel; JS payloads are JS values

ta_datamodel_ecmascript_set_memory_limit.skip: C ECMAScript datamodel; the JS bindings evaluate ECMAScript with their own engine

ta_datamodel_ecmascript_vtable.skip: C ECMAScript datamodel; the JS bindings evaluate ECMAScript with their own engine

ta_datamodel_ecmascript_snapshot.skip: C ECMAScript datamodel; the JS bindings snapshot their own datamodel tables (plain values, encoded with the hibernation codec)

ta_datamodel_ecmascript_restore.skip: C ECMAScript datamodel; the JS bindings restore their own datamodel tables

ta_datamodel_ecmascript_last_error.skip: C ECMAScript datamodel; the JS bindings report what they cannot store themselves

ta_datamodel_ecmascript_wasm_set_time.skip: the clock of the release's tinyactors_datamodel_ecmascript.wasm (browser_wasm.c); the JS bindings do not load the C ECMAScript datamodel, and their own engine reads the platform's clock

ta_host_route_reason.skip: text reason codec for C transports; JS exposes the router reason codes

ta_host_envelope_json.skip: neutral JSON writer for C transports; JS transports use their native JSON codec

ta_host_snapshot_segments.skip: the JS bindings record what every segment ran (sources or image bytes) inside their snapshot, so they know the images to supply without asking the blob

ta_image_event_name.skip: event names reach the bindings as strings (events, effects, _event); the interned name table serves C datamodels and tools

ta_image_ahead_of_time_section.skip: ahead-of-time sections are read by C datamodels; JS datamodels resolve expressions from their source text

ta_http_encode_post.skip: BasicHTTP codec for C hosts without an HTTP stack; JS hosts have fetch/http

ta_http_parse_request.skip: BasicHTTP codec for C hosts without an HTTP stack; JS hosts have fetch/http

ta_runtime_compile_file.skip: OS convenience for C hosts (files); JS hosts read files with their platform

ta_runtime_now_ns.skip: OS convenience for C hosts (clock); JS hosts supply their platform's clock

ta_runtime_resolve.skip: OS convenience for C hosts (file resolver)

ta_runtime_run.skip: OS convenience for C hosts (run with automatic growth); the bindings grow on TA_RUN_EXHAUSTED themselves

ta_runtime_system_free.skip: OS convenience for C hosts (malloc'd systems)

ta_runtime_system_grow.skip: OS convenience for C hosts; the bindings relocate with ta_system_relocate

ta_runtime_system_new.skip: OS convenience for C hosts (malloc'd systems)

ta_system_next_deadline.skip: the next deadline comes with every ta_system_run result (ta_run.next_deadline), which is when the bindings schedule

ta_system_chart_stats_get.skip: the bindings run a ta_host and read per-chart counts host-wide (ta_host_chart_stats), which sums every segment's with this function

ta_system_set_next_serial.skip: for hosts that allocate session ids outside the system (the PostgreSQL binding); ta_host partitions ids per segment itself (and keeps them past the ids of sessions it adopted)

ta_wasm_alloc.skip: the allocator of the release's standalone wasm modules, which import nothing (docs/distribution.md); the web binding is a wasm32-wasi reactor that gives JavaScript the C library's malloc (w_alloc/w_free in bindings/web/src/glue.c) and the library ta_runtime_malloc, and the Node.js addon is native, where wasm.h declares nothing

ta_wasm_free.skip: the allocator of the release's standalone wasm modules (see ta_wasm_alloc); the web binding frees with the C library (w_free in bindings/web/src/glue.c)
